title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 67-69). Grothendieck is working with 'dispositions'. A disposition E is a set E together with a distinguished family Σ_E ⊂ P(E) of parts. Σ_E is a complete lattice (Sup = 'Sup dans Σ_E', presumably the closure/saturation s-η°_E of a union). Each point x has a smallest element S_x = Sup of {x}. In the 'trivial disposition', Σ_E = P(E).

A relation α ⊂ E×E' is the same as a union-preserving map P(E) → P(E'). The generalisation is to study maps α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E' commuting with arbitrary Sup (sup-lattice morphisms). Such an α_* is determined by α: E → Σ_E', x ↦ α_*(S_x).

On this page Grothendieck extends α to α_*(S) = Sup_{x∈S} α(x) = s-η°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)), where ᾱ(S) is the union of the α(x). This works because every S ∈ Σ_E is the Sup of the S_x, x ∈ S. He states as 'Lemme' a bijection Hom_Ens(E, Σ_E') ≅ Hom_ord^!(Σ_E, Σ_E'), where ! means maps preserving arbitrary Sup.

He then wants a 'transpose' of such a map, generalising the converse relation. For trivial dispositions, β is the transpose of α iff x' ∈ α(x) ⇔ x ∈ β(x'). Passing to negations, the condition becomes x' |o| α(x) ⇔ x |o| β(x'), where |o| denotes non-incidence or disjointness.

The next page (Lemme 2) makes this precise. It asks for β_* with α_*(S) |o| S' ⇔ S |o| β_*(S'), and shows the pointwise condition is equivalent to β̄(x') = {x : α(x) |o| x'} lying in Σ_E. This is a transpose relative to an orthogonality relation rather than an order-adjoint.

The margin note doubts the lemma: if A ⊂ E is closed (in Σ_E), is the formula α_*(A) = s-η°(ᾱ(A)) consistent, or only valid under extra conditions?
errors: The lemma as stated is false for a general disposition. Σ_E is a quotient of the free sup-lattice P(E), not free on E. So a map α: E → Σ_E' extends to a Sup-preserving Σ_E → Σ_E' only if it is compatible: whenever S_x ≤ Sup_{y∈T} S_y, α(x) ≤ Sup_{y∈T} α(y). Without this, the formula Sup_{x∈S} α(x) may not respect the order or Sups in Σ_E. The restriction map Hom^!(Σ_E,Σ_E') → Hom(E,Σ_E') is injective but not surjective in general. Grothendieck's own marginal note ('il n'est pas clair que si A fermé…') flags exactly this gap, and the next page adds the compatibility condition (iv).
Minor: the definition α(x) = α_*(Sup Vic°({x})) on p.67 presupposes that the closure of {x} is S_x, which is implicit in the setup.

ideas.what: Correspondences between sets as union-preserving maps P(E)→P(E'), generalised to Sup-preserving maps between lattices of 'closed parts' of dispositions
ideas.modern_name: Category Sup of complete join-semilattices; Rel ≃ free sup-lattice morphisms; Kleisli category of the powerset monad
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lattice theory (Birkhoff; Joyal–Tierney 1984 for Sup as a monoidal category)

ideas.what: Determination of a Sup-map by its values on point-closures S_x
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of free sup-lattice / join-dense generators

ideas.what: Transpose of a correspondence defined via a disjointness/orthogonality relation: α(x) |o| x' ⇔ x |o| β(x'), and for Sup-maps α_*(S) |o| S' ⇔ S |o| β_*(S')
ideas.modern_name: Adjointness with respect to an orthogonality relation; overlap-adjoint in formal topology (Sambin's ≬); involution/dagger structure on Rel and on Chu-space-like morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sambin (basic pairs, overlap relation, 2000s); Chu construction (Barr 1979, Pratt); dagger categories (Selinger, Heunen)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines the transpose of a Sup-map between 'disposition' lattices not as the order-theoretic right adjoint, but by symmetry with respect to the disjointness relation. This is the overlap-symmetric morphism notion later developed in Sambin's formal topology (basic pairs/basic topologies with ≬) and akin to dagger structures on sup-lattice categories. The page records an independent 1986 attempt at a self-dual (dagger-like) category of 'generalised spaces' extending Rel. It is only a sketch, and the condition for existence is worked out on the next page.
missed.quote: On voudrait cependant une notion de transposée d'un tel foncteur, qui généralise le cas connu des "disjoncteurs triviaux" … x' |o| α(x) ⟺ x |o| β(x')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It shows Grothendieck seeking an involutive category of spatial correspondences, a theme now studied via dagger categories and formal topology. It offers no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary sup-lattice theory, and the stated lemma has a gap that Grothendieck himself flags. The only mildly interesting point is the orthogonality-based transpose, which anticipates overlap/dagger notions, but it is a sketch.
transcription_corrections: Line after the formula: the crossed-out word looks like 'fonctoriel' or similar, replaced by 'puisque'; the transcription is plausible.
'Lemme[?]' is underlined; reading 'Lemme' is likely (cf. 'Lemme 2' on the next page).
'd'un tel foncteur[?]' may rather be 'd'un tel foncteur' or 'd'un tel [morphisme]'; uncertain.
The 'disjoncteurs triviaux' reading is uncertain; it may be 'dispositions triviales' as on p.67.
Final line 'Donc donc[?]' is probably 'On a donc' or 'Donc'.
Margin: reads roughly 'Mais il n'est pas clair que si A ⊂ E fermé, α_*(A) = s-η°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)) ? … mais seulement …'.
